items.prompt: Put the story in order.
hints: Think about the start, the middle and the end.
What does Dewi get at the very start?
Find the sentence about the new boots first.
items.explanation: First Dewi gets her boots. Then there is no rain and she is sad. Next the rain comes, and at the end she jumps in a puddle.
items: Dewi is sad because there is no rain.
Grey clouds come and it rains.

items.prompt: What might Dewi do the next time it rains?
hints: Think about how Dewi feels about rain.
What did she do the last time it rained?
People often do a fun thing again.
items.explanation: Dewi loves playing in the rain with her boots. She will probably do it again.

options.text: Put on her boots and play outside.

options.why: Dewi loves rain. She would not hide.
Dewi loves her boots.

items.prompt: Put the story in order.
hints: Start at the beginning of the story.
Find the problem: someone is missing.
End with the happy part.
items.explanation: Bima feeds Pip. Then Pip is missing. Bima hears her in the garden and finds an egg.
items: Pip is not in her box.
Bima hears a cluck in the garden.

items.prompt: Where does Bima look first?
hints: Find the part where Pip is missing.
Bima looks in three places.
Read the first place he looks.
items.explanation: First Bima looks under the table. Then he looks behind the door.

options.why: He looks there next.
He finds Pip there at the end.

items.prompt: What kind of text is 'Frogs'?
hints: Does it tell us true things?
Is there a character with a name?
Does it teach you about frogs?
items.explanation: It gives true facts about frogs, so it is a fact text (non-fiction).

options.why: A story has characters and things that happen to them.
A poem often has rhyme and short lines.

items.prompt: Put a frog's life in order.
hints: Find the part about the mother frog.
What comes out of the egg?
Start with what the mother frog lays.
items.explanation: A frog starts as an egg. A tadpole comes out, grows legs and becomes a little frog.

items.prompt: Put the story in order.
hints: Think about the start, the middle and the end.
Where do they go first?
End with the way home.
items.explanation: They go to the market. Dad buys eggs and rice, Nina picks bananas, then she carries them home.
items: Nina and Dad go to the market.

items.prompt: What happens just after Nina picks the bananas?
hints: Find the part about the bananas.
Read the next sentence.
Look for what Dad does.
items.explanation: After Nina picks the bananas, Dad pays the man.

options.why: That happens before.
That happens at the start.

items.prompt: How do many stories start?
hints: Think about fairy tales.
This is often the very first line.
Which words tell you a story is beginning?
items.explanation: Many stories start with Once upon a time.

options.why: The end is how many stories finish.
Goodbye is what we say when we leave.

items.prompt: Story or fact? Sort the sentences.
hints: Facts are true.
In stories, animals can talk and dance.
Start with: A cow gives us milk. Is it true?
items.explanation: A cow gives us milk and bees make honey are facts. Cows do not dance and bees do not tell jokes, so those are from stories.

items.text: The cow put on a hat and danced.
The bee told the fox a joke.

items.prompt: What picture comes next?

figure.alt: A seed, then a small seedling, then a bigger plant, joined by arrows.

hints: Look at how the plant changes.
It gets bigger each time.
What does a plant grow when it is bigger?
items.explanation: A seed grows into a small plant, then a bigger plant, and then it can grow a flower.

options.why: The seed comes at the start, not the end.
An egg is not part of a plant story.

items.prompt: Read: 'Tom drops his ice cream on the floor.' How will Tom feel?
hints: Think about how you would feel.
Can Tom eat it now?
Find the feeling for when something goes wrong.
items.explanation: Tom cannot eat his ice cream now, so he will probably feel sad.

options.why: Proud is how you feel when you do well.
Dropping food does not make you sleepy.
Brave is how you feel when you face something hard.

items.prompt: Which sentence would come last in a story?
hints: Look at the first words of each sentence.
Some words start stories. Some words end them.
Which one tells what happened after everything else?
items.explanation: From that day on tells us how things ended, so it comes last.

options.text: Once upon a time, there was a fox.
options.why: Once upon a time starts a story.

options.text: One morning, the fox went to the river.
options.why: This sounds like the start or the middle.

options.text: At the river, the fox met a crab.
options.why: This sounds like the middle of a story.

options.text: From that day on, they were best friends.

items.prompt: Ben woke up. He brushed his teeth. Then he ate breakfast. After that he went to school.
hints: Look for the words first, then, and after that.
Put the things in order in your head.
First is at the beginning and last is at the end.
items.explanation: The order is woke up, brushed teeth, ate breakfast, went to school.

parts.prompt: What did Ben do just before school?
What did Ben brush? Write one word.

items.prompt: Put the words first, next and last on the pictures in order.
hints: Look for the picture of the smallest plant.
The seed is first. The big plant is last.
The middle picture shows the next step.
items.explanation: The pictures show a seed first, then a seedling next, then a plant last.

items.prompt: Put the story in order.
hints: What do you do first?
You eat before school.
Waking up comes first.
items.explanation: First I get up, then I eat breakfast, then I go to school.

items.prompt: Put the story in order.
hints: What happens first?
A chick comes out last.
The egg cracks before the chick comes out.
items.explanation: The hen lays an egg, the egg cracks and a chick comes out.

items.prompt: Put the story in order.
hints: What happens first?
Clouds come before rain.
It rains last.
items.explanation: The sun is hot, then dark clouds come, then it rains.

items.prompt: Put the story in order.
hints: Think of a football game.
She kicks before it goes in.
The shout comes last.
items.explanation: She gets the ball, kicks it, it goes in and she shouts.
items: The ball goes into the net.

items.prompt: Put the steps in order to make toast.
hints: You need bread first.
The toast must pop up before you add butter.
Butter comes last.
items.explanation: Get the bread, toast it, wait and then add butter.
items: Wait for it to pop up.

items.prompt: Which is a story?
hints: A story has a character and things that happen.
It tells about a boy or a girl.
Look for the one with something happening.
items.explanation: A story tells about people and what happens to them.

options.text: A boy finds a lost kitten.

options.why: This gives a fact.
This tells you what to do.

items.prompt: Which is a fact text?
hints: A fact text tells us true things.
Look for a sentence about all bees.
It does not have a character.
items.explanation: Bees make honey is a fact.

options.why: This tells what happened to Mia.
This asks someone to do something.

items.prompt: Sort the sentences. Story or fact?
hints: A story is about someone.
A fact is true about many things.
Bo is a person.
items.explanation: Sentences about named people are stories. Sentences about animals or the sun are facts.

items.prompt: What comes first in a story?
hints: A story has three parts.
The first part tells who and where.
It is where the story starts.
items.explanation: The beginning comes first.

options.why: This comes last.
This comes after the beginning.

items.prompt: The end of a story tells what?
hints: Think about the last page of a story.
It tells what happens in the end.
The problem gets solved.
items.explanation: The end tells how the story finishes.

options.why: This is at the start.
The title is at the top.

items.prompt: Which word helps us put things in order?
hints: Order words tell us what comes before and after.
Think of words like next, then and last.
One of the choices is one of them.
items.explanation: First is an order word.

options.why: Red is a colour.
Under tells us where something is.

items.prompt: Which sentence comes last? First, Raj got a seed. Then he planted it. Next he gave it water.
hints: Find the order words.
First, then, next, and one more.
The plant needs time to grow.
items.explanation: A plant grew is the last thing that happened.

options.why: This comes first.
This comes second.

items.prompt: What does Farmer Jo do first?
hints: Find the word first.
Read what comes after it.
It is about the hens.
items.explanation: First, Farmer Jo feeds the hens.

options.why: Farmer Jo does this last.
Farmer Jo does this next.

items.prompt: What does Farmer Jo do after he milks the cow?
hints: Find the word then.
Look at the part after milking.
It is about eggs.
items.explanation: Then he picks up the eggs.

options.why: He did this before.
The story does not say that.

items.prompt: What does Farmer Jo do last?
hints: Find the word last.
It is the final thing.
It is a meal.
items.explanation: Last, Farmer Jo eats his breakfast.

options.why: He did this first.
He did this before breakfast.

items.prompt: Put the farm jobs in order.
hints: Look for order words in the story.
First, next, then and last.
Start with feeding.
items.explanation: The order is hens, cow, eggs, breakfast.

items.prompt: Which word tells us the second job?
hints: The first job uses the word First.
The last job uses the word Last.
Look for the word in between.
items.explanation: Next tells us the second thing that happens.

options.why: First is for the first job.
Last is for the final job.

items.prompt: What comes next? Monday, Tuesday, ___
hints: Say the days of the week.
Monday comes first and Tuesday second.
What is the third day?
items.explanation: Wednesday comes after Tuesday.

options.why: Friday is later in the week.
Sunday is the day before Monday.
